newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end up on results optimism.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end up on results optimism.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on domestic optimism fuelled by expectations of good corporate results in the second half of 1996, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.5 points up at 610.98.

Investors were particularly bullish on plantation shares, due to prospects of strong earnings with tea prices reaching record highs this year, brokers said. Bogawantalawa Plantations rose 15.50 rupees to 50, Kelani Valley 6.50 to 22.75.
"The market...has upside potential of about 650 points by the end of this year," said Deva Ellepola, a broker at Jardine Fleming.

Prospects of a market-friendly budget and the feel-good-factor from the privatisation of Ceylon Steel, where 90 percent was sold for $15 million to South Korea's Hanjung, were also adding to local optimism, brokers said.
Brokers said trading was characterised by a lack of sellers. "Sellers are waiting at higher levels and refusing to budge," said broker Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
Turnover was 10.35 million rupees on 559,995 shares.
